evidences.evidence_quote: In quantum systems, an atom with electrons at high energy levels (i.e., above level 20) is called a Rydberg atom[23].
evidences.evidence_context: For example, to receive 2.4 GHz WiFi signals, the electrons are triggered from energy level 6 to energy level 66. In quantum systems, an atom with electrons at high energy levels (i.e., above level 20) is called a Rydberg atom[23].
evidences.reference_entry: Thomas Gallagher. 2006. Rydberg Atoms. Springer New York, New York, NY, 235–245. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26308-3_14
evidences.why_this_judgment_zh: 引用[23]仅用于定义Rydberg原子，是标准术语引用，不涉及任何亚毫米级感知能力或振动检测。根据严格规则，属于false_positive。 原文证据句引用了其他编号，没有引用目标论文编号。

evidences.evidence_quote: Based on the Schrödinger equation [23], E′(t) can be measured in both macroscopic and microscopic perspectives.
evidences.evidence_context: From the macroscopic perspective, conventional receivers receive RF signals using antennas. From the microscopic perspective, quantum receiver received RF signals using the electron energy transition of atoms. Based on the Schrödinger equation [23], E′(t) can be measured in both macroscopic and microscopic perspectives.
